validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via 3 independent-era documents. (1) A 2001 wire announcement ('Falcon Gas Storage to start construction on Hill-Lake pipeline') syndicated verbatim on both www.oilandgasonline.com and www.hydrocarbononline.com (same story, same publisher network -- counted as ONE origin, not two): 'Falcon Gas Storage Company and its subsidiary, Hill-Lake Gas Storage, L.P., today announced that right-of-way acquisition has been completed for the construction of a new 17-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline in Eastland County near Dallas/Ft. Worth... Falcon's Hill-Lake Pipeline will operate at a maximum pressure of 1200 psig and will have a maximum capacity of more than 300,000 Mcf per day. The new pipeline will connect Falcon's Hill-Lake Gas Storage Facility with both the Lone Star Pipeline Company's Line X and the El Paso/TXU Fuels North Texas Pipeline.' (2) www.nortexmidstream.com/facilities -- current URL, HTTP 200 with the requested content per url_verifier, but the live page now REDIRECTS to https://www.williams.com/pipeline/nortex-storage, i.e. NorTex Midstream's storage assets (including Hill-Lake) are now operated by Williams Companies. That current page confirms: 'Hill-Lake Gas Storage Facility... Eastland County, Texas... Working Gas Capacity: 10 Bcf... Maximum Daily Withdrawal: 350,000 Mcf/d... Maximum Daily Injection: 350,000 Mcf/d... connects to the Atmos Line X and the North Texas Pipeline' -- i.e. the SAME two interconnecting systems named in 2001 (Lone Star's Line X became Atmos Line X after Atmos acquired the Lone Star/TXU Gas system; Atmos Pipeline Texas is GEM row P0369). This independently corroborates the facility and its two named interconnects are still active today, 20+ years after construction. (3) PR Newswire, 'Tailwater Capital to Acquire NorTex Midstream Partners' (2021-02-17): confirms NorTex Midstream (owner of the Hill-Lake storage/pipeline complex) was previously owned by Castleton Commodities International (CCI) and was acquired by Tailwater Capital LLC in 2021; describes NorTex as operating '83 miles of natural gas transmission pipelines' and storage that has 'operated consistently for nearly 60 years' -- the release does not name Hill-Lake specifically, so it corroborates the corporate/ownership chain (Falcon -> ... -> CCI -> Tailwater -> [now] Williams) rather than the pipeline's own specs, but it is a genuinely independent document from a different era. CLASSIFICATION: correct. This is a natural gas transmission connector pipeline (not a gathering or plant-process line) linking a storage facility to two mainline gas transmission systems -- properly filed in GGIT as a transmission pipeline. DUPLICATE: none found. Checked the full 45-row TX-operating roster; no other row names Hill Lake, Falcon Gas Storage, NorTex, Line X, or the North Texas Pipeline as its own identity. P4416 (Worsham-Steed Pipeline) has a superficially similar profile (short line, huge nominal capacity number typical of a storage-connector), but nothing ties it to the same physical facility -- not flagged. ATTRIBUTION: Owner/Operator is not an owed unit on this row's worklist (handled on the separate Pipeline operators/owners tab, out of scope here); noting for that tab's future pass: current operator per the Williams redirect is Williams Companies (via the NorTex Storage business), successor to Tailwater Capital (2021) / Castleton Commodities International / originally Falcon Gas Storage Company (2001). SPEC: Status=operating -- confirmed (the Williams/NorTex facility page describes Hill-Lake as a live, in-service storage facility with current capacity figures, i.e. its interconnecting pipeline is presumptively still in service; no indication of abandonment or replacement). Fuel=Gas -- confirmed (explicitly a 'natural gas pipeline'). ConstructionYear=2001 -- confirmed exactly ('Construction is scheduled to start the first week of August' 2001, 'expected to be operational by November 1' 2001). LengthKnown=17.00 mi -- confirmed exactly ('17-mile... natural gas pipeline'). Diameter=20 in -- confirmed exactly ('20-inch diameter'). Capacity=300,000.00 Mcf/d -- confirmed exactly and explicitly attributed to the PIPELINE itself, not just the storage facility: 'Falcon's Hill-Lake Pipeline will operate at a maximum pressure of 1200 psig and will have a maximum capacity of more than 300,000 Mcf per day.' Note for calibration: this is the pipeline's ORIGINAL 2001 design/nameplate capacity; the storage FACILITY's own withdrawal/injection capacity has since grown to 350,000 Mcf/d per the current Williams page -- that is a different asset (the storage wells/compression, not the 17-mile connector) and from a different date, so it is not a conflict with GEM's Capacity value, just a nuance worth knowing if this pipeline is ever re-surveyed for a post-2001 capacity expansion. StartState/Province=Texas, EndState/Province=Texas, StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=United States -- confirmed (Eastland County, Texas throughout; a short intra-county connector). CAVEAT ON TIER: the specific numeric values (length/diameter/pipeline-capacity/construction date) rest on ONE original source (the 2001 wire story, mirrored on two trade-press domains that are the same publisher network, not independent of each other) -- I could not find a second, numerically-independent source restating those exact figures (FERC eLibrary, Texas RRC, PHMSA/NPMS and EIA were not reachable/searchable in this session -- WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-task and Google/DuckDuckGo scripted queries returned JS-shell/no-results pages). Staging tier=medium accordingly rather than high, though nothing found conflicts with the sheet. HARVESTED CITATION POOL: all 3 citations harvested from this row's gem.wiki page were opened and read (oilandgasonline.com 2001 announcement; nortexmidstream.com/facilities; PR Newswire Tailwater/NorTex acquisition) -- 3 of 3, 100% coverage.
